segments.en: Hello, everyone, and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Katrin, and today we've got some kids for you in this dialogue.
segments.zh: 我的名字是卡特琳，今天我们在这次对话中为您准备了一些孩子。

segments.en: They're doing something that's very common in America.
segments.zh: 他们正在做一些在美国很常见的事情。

segments.en: I'm not so sure if it's common elsewhere, but we'll find that out later.
segments.zh: 我不太确定它是否在其他地方很常见，但我们稍后会发现。

segments.en: So today we're going to ask for money because we are having a fundraiser.
segments.zh: 所以今天我们要要钱，因为我们有筹款活动。

segments.en: So this is a very interesting word.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个非常有趣的词。

segments.en: Why don't we take a look at it in Vocabulary Preview?
segments.zh: 我们为什么不在词汇预览中看一下呢？

segments.en: So a fundraiser is a thing.
segments.zh: 所以筹款活动是一回事。

segments.en: It's an event.
segments.zh: 这是一个事件。

segments.en: It's something that you do at a school or a business to try and collect money for a special event or charity.
segments.zh: 这是您在学校或企业中尝试为特殊活动或慈善机构筹集资金的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So money, you can also say is funds, right?
segments.zh: 所以钱，你也可以说是资金，对吧？

segments.en: And that's what you're trying to do.
segments.zh: 这就是你正在尝试做的事情。

segments.en: You're trying to collect.
segments.zh: 你正在尝试收集。

segments.en: You're trying to gather a lot of money or funds in order for, like you say, some sort of objective purpose.
segments.zh: 你正试图收集大量的钱或资金，就像你说的那样，为了某种客观目的。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it's not just like we're having a fundraiser to earn more profits this year.
segments.zh: 因此，这不只是我们今年有筹款活动来赚取更多利润。

segments.en: It's usually an event that's for some kind of charity or good cause.
segments.zh: 这通常是出于某种慈善或公益事业的活动。

segments.en: So for example, the company is having a fundraiser for Jenny's child because he's sick and they can't pay for medical care.
segments.zh: 例如，该公司正在为珍妮的孩子筹款，因为他生病了，他们无法支付医疗费用。

segments.en: So a fundraiser is for a good cause.
segments.zh: 因此，筹款活动是为了一个好的原因。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So that's what this dialogue is all about today.
segments.zh: 所以这就是今天这个对话的全部内容。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to the dialogue for the first time and we'll be back in a bit.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不第一次听对话，我们会回来的。

segments.en: Okay, Mark, it's your turn to ring the doorbell.
segments.zh: 好吧，马克，轮到你按门铃了。

segments.en: I did it last time.
segments.zh: 我上次做的。

segments.en: I hate going door to door and I hate asking for money.
segments.zh: 我讨厌挨家挨户，我讨厌要钱。

segments.en: But we need to raise enough money for the school fundraiser so that our class can win the pizza party.
segments.zh: 但我们需要为学校筹款活动筹集足够的资金，以便我们的班级能够赢得比萨派对。

segments.en: You do want to have a pizza party, don't you?
segments.zh: 你确实想举办披萨派对，不是吗？

segments.en: Yes, but...
segments.zh: 是，可是……

segments.en: Just go already.
segments.zh: 你赶紧走吧。

segments.en: No one's coming.
segments.zh: 没人来。

segments.en: Try again.
segments.zh: 再试一次。

segments.en: Maybe there's no one home.
segments.zh: 也许家里没人。

segments.en: Of course there's someone home.
segments.zh: 当然有人在家。

segments.en: There are two cars in the driveway and I can see lights on in the house.
segments.zh: 车道上有两辆车，我可以看到房子里的灯亮着。

segments.en: Hello?
segments.zh: 喂？

segments.en: Anybody home?
segments.zh: 有人在家吗？

segments.en: We would like to know if you want to sponsor us in our school fundraiser.
segments.zh: 我们想知道您是否想在我们的学校筹款活动中赞助我们。

segments.en: 50% of the profits go towards the new school playground.
segments.zh: 50%的利润用于新学校操场。

segments.en: I don't know why anyone would want what's in this catalogue anyway.
segments.zh: 我不知道为什么有人会想要这个目录中的内容。

segments.en: It's just a bunch of tacky Christmas ornaments.
segments.zh: 这只是一堆俗气的圣诞装饰品。

segments.en: CDs of old people singing Christmas songs and special crackers and cheeses and boxes of chocolate.
segments.zh: 还有老年人唱圣诞歌的 CD、特色饼干和奶酪，以及盒装巧克力。

segments.en: You don't like chocolate?
segments.zh: 你不喜欢巧克力？

segments.en: Not this kind.
segments.zh: 不喜欢这种。

segments.en: They've got weird names like ganache and praline.
segments.zh: 他们有像甘纳许和普拉林这样奇怪的名字。

segments.en: Look, I just saw someone walking around inside.
segments.zh: 看，我刚刚看到有人在里面走来走去。

segments.en: These people are being very rude.
segments.zh: 这些人非常粗鲁。

segments.en: Finally, someone's coming.
segments.zh: 终于有人来了。

segments.en: They don't look too happy.
segments.zh: 他们看起来不太高兴。

segments.en: Hi, sir.
segments.zh: 您好，先生。

segments.en: Would you like to sponsor us or make a donation to...
segments.zh: 您想赞助我们还是捐款给...

segments.en: What grade are you kids in?
segments.zh: 你们孩子在什么年级？

segments.en: Grade 7.
segments.zh: 七年级。

segments.en: Then for goodness sake, don't you see this sign?
segments.zh: 那么看在上帝的份上，你没有看到这个标志吗？

segments.en: Can't you read?
segments.zh: 你不识字吗？

segments.en: No soliciting.
segments.zh: 谢绝推销及募捐。

segments.en: Alright, so obviously the kids are selling candy and a lot of different things for their new playground.
segments.zh: 好吧，显然孩子们正在为他们的新游乐场出售糖果和许多不同的东西。

segments.en: That's the fundraiser, right?
segments.zh: 这就是筹款活动，对吧？

segments.en: So they use a lot of interesting words and phrases there.
segments.zh: 所以他们在那里使用了很多有趣的单词和短语。

segments.en: Why don't we take a look at a couple of them on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不看看他们中的一些语言外卖。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Well, the first word is one that Marco, you've already talked a little bit about today.
segments.zh: 好吧，第一个词是 Marco，你今天已经谈过一些。

segments.en: We talked about fundraiser, to raise.
segments.zh: 我们谈到了筹款，筹集。

segments.en: Well, we do have the verb here, to raise enough money.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们确实有动词在这里筹集足够的钱。

segments.en: So raise is a verb that means to collect or gather or to get.
segments.zh: 所以 raise 是一个动词，意思是收集或收集或获取。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you wouldn't really say we are collecting money or we are gathering money.
segments.zh: 所以你不会真的说我们在收钱，或者我们正在收集钱。

segments.en: You say we are raising money for the victims of the earthquake in Haiti.
segments.zh: 你说我们正在为海地地震的受害者筹集资金。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And the reason we don't say we are earning money is because you're not doing any work.
segments.zh: 我们不说我们赚钱的原因是因为你没有做任何工作。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Really, you're not going to the job at 9 o'clock and leaving the job at 5 o'clock.
segments.zh: 真的，你不会在 9 点钟去上班，而在 5 点钟离开工作。

segments.en: You're actually asking people for donations.
segments.zh: 你实际上是在向人们索要捐款。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So that's what you're doing.
segments.zh: 所以这就是你正在做的事情。

segments.en: You are raising money.
segments.zh: 你在筹集资金。

segments.en: And now moving on, another way that you can help people maybe through a charity or donation is also to sponsor.
segments.zh: 现在继续前进，您可以通过慈善或捐赠帮助人们的另一种方式也是赞助。

segments.en: To sponsor someone or something.
segments.zh: 赞助某人或某事。

segments.en: Okay, so people can sponsor events or people and companies can also do this as well.
segments.zh: 好的，所以人们可以赞助活动或人员，公司也可以这样做。

segments.en: So to sponsor someone is basically to give them money in support of a cause.
segments.zh: 所以赞助某人基本上就是给他们钱来支持一个事业。

segments.en: For example, have you ever done one of those 5K runs or 10K runs?
segments.zh: 例如，您是否曾经进行过这些 5k 运行或 10k 运行之一？

segments.en: Did you have to collect sponsors basically to find people who would help pay money for you to do this run?
segments.zh: 您是否必须基本上收集赞助商才能找到愿意帮助您支付费用的人来进行这项工作？

segments.en: Not personally, but I know people who have, who actually get companies interested and maybe that person, for example, is going to run 5K in this race in order to raise money for victims of some serious illness.
segments.zh: 不是个人，但我知道有人，他们实际上让公司感兴趣，例如，那个人会在这场比赛中跑 5k，以便为患有严重疾病的受害者筹集资金。

segments.en: And so they get sponsors, they get companies to donate money for this cause.
segments.zh: 所以他们得到了赞助商，他们让公司为这个事业捐款。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: You could have a person or a company sponsor you, they could be your sponsor by giving you money that you can then use for this charity or special cause.
segments.zh: 您可以让一个人或公司赞助您，他们可以通过给您钱来作为您的赞助商，然后您可以将其用于此慈善事业或特殊事业。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So the difference between a fundraiser and to sponsor something or someone is that sponsoring is not always for a charity or for some sort of non-profit cause, right?
segments.zh: 因此，筹款活动和赞助某人或某人之间的区别在于，赞助并不总是为了慈善机构或某种非营利事业，对吧？

segments.en: We have many sponsors for concerts or for sporting events.
segments.zh: 我们有许多赞助商参加音乐会或体育赛事。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So oftentimes when you see athletes, they have their sponsors or their sponsors logos written all over their jerseys, the clothes that they wear.
segments.zh: 所以很多时候，当你看到运动员时，他们的球衣上到处都是他们的赞助商或赞助商的标志，他们穿的衣服。

segments.en: So for example, if you're watching Formula One racing, you see the Ferrari and the bank emblems and all these different things.
segments.zh: 例如，如果您正在观看一级方程式赛车，您会看到法拉利和银行标志以及所有这些不同的东西。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So those are different ways of sponsoring events or people.
segments.zh: 所以这些是赞助活动或人的不同方式。

segments.en: And now moving on, we have a word that's not really related to money and fundraisers, but it's a very interesting word and very common.
segments.zh: 现在继续，我们有一个与金钱和筹款活动无关的词，但这是一个非常有趣的词，非常普遍。

segments.en: When the kids mention that they're selling a bunch of tacky Christmas ornaments.
segments.zh: 当孩子们提到他们正在出售一堆俗气的圣诞装饰品时。

segments.en: Tacky.
segments.zh: 俗气。

segments.en: Tacky.
segments.zh: 俗气。

segments.en: So we're going to hear this a lot and the interesting thing about the word tacky is that it means something different to everyone.
segments.zh: 所以我们会经常听到这个词，关于俗气这个词的有趣之处在于它对每个人都有不同的意义。

segments.en: So what I think is tacky might be just normal for Marco and what Marco thinks is really tacky might be something that I actually like.
segments.zh: 所以我认为俗气的东西对马可来说可能是正常的，而马可认为真的俗气可能是我真正喜欢的东西。

segments.en: And so tacky is basically a bad thing.
segments.zh: 所以俗气基本上是一件坏事。

segments.en: It means something is not good looking or not very fashionable.
segments.zh: 这意味着有些东西不好看或不太时尚。

segments.en: It's like in bad taste.
segments.zh: 这就像不好的味道。

segments.en: But as you say, taste is something subjective, right?
segments.zh: 但正如你所说，品味是主观的，对吧？

segments.en: So maybe for example, sometimes we say that when girls wear too much makeup, it's very tacky, bright red lipstick and blue eyeshadow.
segments.zh: 所以也许例如，有时我们会说，当女孩化妆太多时，它是非常俗气的，鲜红色的唇膏和蓝色的眼影。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So a guy might say, oh, that's so tacky.
segments.zh: 所以一个人可能会说，哦，太俗气了。

segments.en: Whereas another person might not think it's tacky at all.
segments.zh: 而另一个人可能根本不认为它很俗气。

segments.en: So this happens a lot and we use this word a lot with decorations, for example, for someone's house, you may describe it as tacky or a restaurant or a bar.
segments.zh: 所以这种情况经常发生，我们经常将这个词与装饰品一起使用，例如，对于某人的房子，您可以将其描述为俗气、餐厅或酒吧。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So for maybe sometimes those Italian restaurants that have the red and white checkered table claws and the pictures of the Italians with the mustaches, I might think that's a little bit tacky.
segments.zh: 因此，有时对于那些有红白格纹桌爪和意大利人留着胡须的照片的意大利餐厅，我可能会认为这有点俗气。

segments.en: But maybe you think it's cute.
segments.zh: 但也许你认为它很可爱。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So something that's tacky.
segments.zh: 所以有些俗气的东西。

segments.en: And as we say, people use it all the time.
segments.zh: 正如我们所说，人们一直在使用它。

segments.en: And it's not necessarily a bad thing.
segments.zh: 这不一定是坏事。

segments.en: You can just say, oh, it's a little bit tacky or I think this thing is a little bit tacky.
segments.zh: 你可以说，哦，有点俗气，或者我认为这东西有点俗气。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And that's it, right?
segments.zh: 就这些了，对吧？

segments.en: So a little bit of a language takeaway, towards the end of the dialogue, when the kids were reading the sign, the sign said, no soliciting.
segments.zh: 于是一点点的语言外卖，在对话快结束时，当孩子们在读标志时，标志上说，没有请求。

segments.en: And they didn't understand what that means.
segments.zh: 他们不明白这意味着什么。

segments.en: What does it mean when you have a sign that says no soliciting?
segments.zh: 当你有一个不招揽的标志是什么意思？

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So to solicit is to try to sell something or to offer a service.
segments.zh: 所以招揽就是尝试卖东西或提供服务。

segments.en: So basically the sign means, please don't come to my house and sell me stuff.
segments.zh: 所以基本上标志意味着，请不要来我家卖东西。

segments.en: For example, we have door to door insurance salesmen or makeup salespeople.
segments.zh: 例如，我们有挨家挨户的保险推销员或化妆品销售人员。

segments.en: And these people go to your door and they try to sell you their product.
segments.zh: 这些人走到你家门口，他们试图向你推销他们的产品。

segments.en: And no soliciting means, don't come to my house.
segments.zh: 没有征求的意思，不要来我家。

segments.en: I'm not going to answer the door if you're trying to sell something.
segments.zh: 如果你想卖东西，我不会开门。

segments.en: So to solicit is to try and sell something.
segments.zh: 所以招揽就是尝试卖东西。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: But usually in person, trying to make a sale uninvited, right?
segments.zh: 但通常是面对面，试图不请自来销售，对吧？

segments.en: Because if you're a businessman and you have a meeting, a sales meeting, you're not really soliciting with that other person.
segments.zh: 因为如果你是一个商人并且你有一个会议，一个销售会议，你并没有真正与那个人招揽。

segments.en: No, this is basically trying to sell something to a stranger.
segments.zh: 不，这基本上是想向陌生人推销东西。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And well, going back, when we were talking about no soliciting, you said that salespeople go door to door selling things.

segments.en: So this is an interesting phrase and it's a fixed phrase, going door to door.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个有趣的短语，它是一个固定的短语，挨家挨户。

segments.en: Well, think about it.

segments.en: So a salesperson who wants to sell maybe some makeup goes to one house and no one wants to buy any makeup there.

segments.en: So she goes to the next house.

segments.en: But we don't really say house to house because she's going to your door to offer the makeup.
segments.zh: 但我们并没有真正说是挨家挨户，因为她会去你家门口化妆。

segments.en: So we just say going door to door.
segments.zh: 所以我们只是说挨家挨户。

segments.en: That means going to strangers' homes in order, one door after the next, to sell something.
segments.zh: 这意味着要按顺序去陌生人的家中，一扇门后，卖东西。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: You go door to door.

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And now we have an interesting question and it's a very good one because it's a question that comes up a lot.
segments.zh: 现在我们有一个有趣的问题，这是一个非常好的问题，因为这是一个经常出现的问题。

segments.en: When somebody asks you, if you're studying for example, what grade are you in?
segments.zh: 当有人问你时，例如，如果你在学习，你在什么年级？

segments.en: Okay, what grade are you in?
segments.zh: 好吧，你在什么年级？

segments.en: So in the American system, for example, we have the very, very bottom, grade K, which is kindergarten for maybe a five-year-old.
segments.zh: 例如，在美国系统中，我们有非常、非常低级的 K 级，它可能是一个五岁的孩子的幼儿园。

segments.en: And at the very top, we have high school, grade 12.
segments.zh: 在最顶端，我们有高中，12年级。

segments.en: And so in between we have one, two, three, four, five, you know, and up.
segments.zh: 所以在这两者之间，我们有一、二、三、四、五，你知道的，甚至向上。

segments.en: And so basically to find out what year in school a student is, you have to ask him or her, what grade are you in?
segments.zh: 所以基本上要找出一个学生在学校的哪一年，你必须问他或她，你在什么年级？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So then the person would say, I'm in sixth grade, I'm in eighth grade.
segments.zh: 那么那个人会说，我在六年级，我在八年级。

segments.en: But this is the way you ask this question for school as you said, a kid that's maybe five years old all the way to 18 years old in high school.
segments.zh: 但正如你所说，这就是你在学校问这个问题的方式，一个可能 5 岁到 18 岁的孩子在高中。

segments.en: What grade are you in?
segments.zh: 你在什么年级？

segments.en: Now if you're in university and you want to ask your friend what year of university that person's in, then you say, what year are you?
segments.zh: 现在，如果你在上大学，想问你的朋友那个人在哪一年上大学，那么你说，你是哪一年的？

segments.en: What year are you?
segments.zh: 你是哪一年的？

segments.en: Yeah, you don't say grade.
segments.zh: 是的，你不说年级。

segments.en: So basically grade refers to like what you said, Marco, those first 12 years of school.
segments.zh: 所以基本上年级是指你说的，马可，上学的前12年。

segments.en: And so we call them, we thought, no, we don't call it grade 12.
segments.zh: 所以我们称他们为他们，我们认为，不，我们不称它为 12 年级。

segments.en: So you could ask anybody under the age of 18, what grade are you in?
segments.zh: 所以你可以问一个 18 岁以下的人，你在什么年级？

segments.en: But when you go to university or when you're talking about university students, it gets a little bit different.
segments.zh: 但是当你上大学或谈论大学生时，情况会有所不同。

segments.en: So you can say, what year are you in or what year are you?
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，你在哪一年或者你是哪一年？

segments.en: So if you're not sure about someone's age and you maybe think they're in college, you can ask them, what year are you?
segments.zh: 因此，如果您不确定某人的年龄并且您可能认为他们在大学，您可以问他们，您是哪一年的？

segments.en: But generally anyone under 18, what grade are you in?
segments.zh: 但一般来说，18 岁以下的人，你在什么年级？

segments.en: Okay, good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And our last phrase, and this is kind of an expression, right?
segments.zh: 还有我们的最后一句话，这是一种表达方式，对吧？

segments.en: Right, for goodness sake.
segments.zh: 对，看在上帝的份上。

segments.en: So this is an expression that's used to indicate maybe you're a little bit frustrated.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个表达式，用于表示您可能有点沮丧。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.zh: 好吧，所以挨家挨户的推销员。

segments.en: I think this used to be a very American thing.
segments.zh: 我认为这曾经是一个非常美国的事情。

segments.en: I think back in the 50s, you would always see movies where this was actually a profession.
segments.zh: 我想在 50 年代，你总是会看到这实际上是一种职业的电影。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: People would go door-to-door selling hairbrushes or magazine subscriptions, pretty much everything.
segments.zh: 人们会挨家挨户地出售发刷或杂志订阅，几乎所有东西。

segments.en: Yeah, you still see it sometimes.
segments.zh: 是的，你有时仍然会看到它。

segments.en: But I think it was much more popular in the 1950s because people didn't really use their phones as much to sell things.
segments.zh: 但我认为它在 1950 年代更受欢迎，因为人们并没有真正使用手机来卖东西。

segments.zh: 有人把他的车开到你附近然后去每一个房子都更便宜。

segments.zh: 但是，是的，这是一项非常有趣的工作。

segments.en: And also, I think, well, now maybe that's been reduced a lot because now you have the internet.

segments.en: Oh yeah, well the internet means that the salespeople come to you without you having to get up.

segments.en: But it's very interesting because I remember you would have all these door-to-door salesmen.

segments.zh: 我不知道，在美国，正如你所说，这不再很常见了。
